guide.verdict: Easiest: Internal tool for your own Zendesk account (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Multi-customer app (global OAuth + review) (app review).

composio.note: Composio lists Zendesk as managed OAuth, fine for prototypes. Check the toolkit page for which methods are managed.

need_own_app.answer: For prototypes, Composio's managed app works. For production with outside customers, plan on your own OAuth client, because managed apps show Composio's name on consent and share quota. Zendesk also requires distributed apps to be reviewed.

prerequisites.title: Zendesk account on a supported plan
prerequisites.detail: A Zendesk account is needed to get a client ID, and OAuth clients are created in Admin Center.

prerequisites.title: Decide client kind
prerequisites.detail: New clients must be set to Public or Confidential; public clients must use PKCE.

steps.title: Create OAuth client in Admin Center
steps.detail: Go to Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients and click Add OAuth client. Choose the client kind, then save and copy the secret immediately.
steps.done_when: You have a client identifier and the full secret saved.

steps.title: Check redirect URI format
steps.detail: Confirm the redirect URL is absolute and https (except localhost). Use the Zendesk core subdomain, not a host-mapped one.
steps.done_when: The redirect URI passes these checks.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, using the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: The auth config exists and a test connection works.

steps.title: Configure token expiry handling
steps.detail: Handle refresh tokens and re-run the full OAuth flow when one expires. Older clients must pass expires_in or no refresh token is issued.
steps.done_when: Token refresh works in a test.

steps.title: Request global OAuth client
steps.detail: Apps working across many Zendesk accounts must request a global OAuth client. Email platformteam@zendesk.com if it takes longer than expected.
steps.done_when: Zendesk confirms the global OAuth client.

steps.title: Submit app for Zendesk review
steps.detail: Submit the app and, if listing, your Marketplace profile with the required fields. Profile is reviewed together with the app on first submission.

traps.title: Secret is shown in full only once
traps.detail: After saving, only the first nine characters are accessible. Copy it immediately.

traps.title: Tokens expire and refresh needs new requests
traps.detail: Refresh tokens last 30 days by default (7-90 days) and expire. Existing tokens cannot be refreshed.

traps.title: Public client without PKCE breaks
traps.detail: Switching an existing client to public before implementing PKCE stops it working.

traps.title: Authorization code expires in 120 seconds
traps.detail: Exchange the code quickly after the user authorizes.

traps.title: Expire tokens setting is permanent
traps.detail: Once enabled it cannot be turned off.

traps.title: Customer credentials no longer allowed
traps.detail: Distributed apps must use global OAuth, not a customer's credentials.

blockers.symptom: Global OAuth request pending with no response
blockers.what_it_means: Zendesk gives no fixed time; it depends on queue and time of week.
blockers.what_to_do: Email platformteam@zendesk.com if it takes longer than expected.

blockers.what_it_means: Older clients must pass expires_in so access tokens expire.

evidence.answer: OAuth clients are managed in Zendesk Admin Center under Apps and integrations > APIs > OAuth clients.

evidence.answer: To use OAuth authentication, the developer must register their application with Zendesk.

evidence.answer: A new OAuth client is created by clicking Add OAuth client in the OAuth client list.

evidence.answer: The page lists these plans for the Suites product line (this article's plan requirement): Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, or Enterprise Plus.

evidence.answer: The page lists these plans for the Support product line (this article's plan requirement): Team, Professional, or Enterprise.

evidence.question: G1

evidence.answer: Existing OAuth clients created before the kind setting currently have kind set to unknown and stay unaffected until the kind is updated.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: is April 1, 2027.
evidence.answer: For existing local (non-global) OAuth clients, the deadline to adopt the refresh token flow is April 1, 2027.

evidence.question: G1

evidence.answer: If the admin who created an OAuth client loses the permissions needed to manage OAuth clients, the client stays active.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: You must register your application to generate OAuth credentials that your application can
evidence.answer: Client registration is not automatic: the developer must register the application to generate OAuth credentials.

evidence.question: G2

evidence.answer: The page describes a single-account OAuth client for one Zendesk account; apps working across many Zendesk accounts can request a global OAuth client instead.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Other users can also continue to authorize the application and obtain new
evidence.answer: For authorization_code tokens, other users can also keep authorizing the application and obtain new tokens, even if the admin who created the client loses access.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The Zendesk authorization page opens in the end user's browser.
evidence.answer: Each end user authorizes the app on the Zendesk authorization page, which opens in the end user's browser.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Scopes - Select the scopes this client can request. Leave this field empty to
evidence.answer: The scopes field lets the developer select which scopes the client can request; leaving it empty allows all scopes.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The read scope gives an app access to GET endpoints, including permission to sideload related resources.

evidence.question: G4

evidence.answer: The write scope gives an app access to POST, PUT, and DELETE endpoints, for creating, updating, and deleting resources.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The impersonate scope allows a Zendesk admin to make requests on behalf of end
evidence.answer: The impersonate scope allows a Zendesk admin to make requests on behalf of end users.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: "scope": "tickets:read"
evidence.answer: Scopes can be narrowed to specific resources using the resource:scope syntax, for example tickets:read.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: active tokens and refreshed tokens are not retroactively affected.
evidence.answer: Scope restrictions apply only to newly generated access tokens; existing active and refreshed tokens are not retroactively affected.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: The default, minimum, and maximum expiration times are:
evidence.answer: Default, minimum, and maximum token lifetimes are listed: access token default 30 minutes, minimum 5 minutes, maximum 48 hours; refresh token default 30 days, minimum 7 days, maximum 90 days.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: between 300 seconds (5 minutes) and 172,800 seconds (2 days).
evidence.answer: When requesting an access token, expires_in must be between 300 seconds (5 minutes) and 172,800 seconds (2 days).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Specify a value between 604,800 seconds (7 days) and 7,776,000 seconds (90 days).
evidence.answer: When requesting a refresh token, refresh_token_expires_in must be between 604,800 seconds (7 days) and 7,776,000 seconds (90 days).

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: The authorization code is only valid for 120 seconds.
evidence.answer: The authorization code is valid for only 120 seconds.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: full OAuth authorization flow again.
evidence.answer: Refresh tokens also expire; if one expires or is invalid, the app must send the user through the full OAuth authorization flow again.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: expires_in in your authorization requests.
evidence.answer: Clients created before refresh token support must include expires_in in authorization requests, otherwise access tokens do not expire and refresh tokens do not work.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: This setting is permanent and cannot be turned off once enabled.
evidence.answer: Enabling the Expire tokens setting gives all tokens from that client a default expiration, and this setting cannot be turned off once enabled.

evidence.answer: The page's plan listing for the Suites product line includes Team, Growth, Professional, Enterprise, and Enterprise Plus; the page does not state prices or fees.

items.reason: Quote states registration is required to generate OAuth credentials.
Quote says the changes do not apply to customers developing for internal use.
Quote says all apps for distribution to Zendesk customers, listed or not, must be submitted for review and approval.
Quote says all public integrations must go through Marketplace review.
Quote confirms enhanced security reviews are required but does not say what they check, so the statement's 'what they check is not stated' is consistent; the quote supports the requirement itself.
Quote says developers can request a global OAuth client.
Quote says the duration is hard to state and depends on pending requests and time of week.
Quote says to email platformteam@zendesk.com if a request takes longer than expected.
Quote says customers using API-token apps must approve global OAuth when the developer makes it available.
Quote says developers must use global OAuth and are no longer permitted to use customer credentials.
Quote states every API call must include source-identifying headers.
Quote says developers must conform to rules on handling customer data to prevent misuse or unauthorized exposure.
Table gives default 30 days, minimum 7 days, maximum 90 days for refresh tokens.
Quote says clients created before refresh token support must explicitly pass expires_in during authorization.
Quote only fragments 'full OAuth authorization flow again' without stating the condition of expiry or invalidity; cannot confirm the trigger.
Quote says the profile is reviewed in conjunction with the first app or theme submission.
Quote says to enter a company contact the Zendesk team can reach to escalate to sales or support.
Quote says refresh tokens are granted on new requests and existing tokens cannot be refreshed.
Quote states the authorization code is valid for 120 seconds.
Quote says the setting is permanent and cannot be turned off once enabled.
Quotes say internal-use apps are outside the review changes and the app must be registered for OAuth credentials; no provider review is stated as required.
Quotes support registering the OAuth client, but do not establish the full ordered steps before customers can connect.
Quotes list plans but do not state a builder prerequisite about needing a listed plan for this setup.
Quotes state apps for distribution to multiple customers must be submitted for review and approval and go through Marketplace review.
Quotes require review for distributed/public apps; 'always' is consistent but the quotes do not explicitly say the review is always required for every case.
Quotes support the review and approval step, but do not state the ordered sequence including requesting the global OAuth client and submitting for review.
Quotes say the review covers safety and security guidelines and Marketplace conformance; 'your listing' is roughly covered by conformance to standards, but is not stated explicitly.
Quote says customers using API-token apps must approve global OAuth when the developer makes it available.
Quotes state developers must follow customer data rules and include source headers on every API call.

Quotes support internal tools needing only registration and multi-customer apps needing review and global OAuth with an undocumented wait; the 'about an hour' and 'no wait' timing for internal tools is not in the quotes.
